title: Dynamic Programming
summary: **Dynamic programming** saves smaller answers so later states can reuse them.

blocks.prompt: What should a DP trace check first?
choices: The state that proves the next move
The final button the user clicks
The color of the code editor
blocks.why: Check what one table entry means first. A recurrence is hard to debug when the state meaning is vague.

sections.title: When DP helps
sections.summary: Use dynamic programming when many branches ask the same smaller question and saved answers prevent repeated work.

blocks.title: When to use this
blocks.body: Use dynamic programming when many branches ask the same smaller question and saved answers prevent repeated work.

blocks.prompt: Which debugging habit fits dynamic programming best?
choices: Trace one small state change before trying a larger input
Start with the largest hidden case
Change the data structure after each failed test
Ignore the saved state and read only the final answer
blocks.why: A tiny table exposes whether the recurrence is reading the right earlier cells before large inputs hide the error.

sections.title: Common DP mistakes
sections.summary: DP code often fails when the base case is correct but the fill order reads a state that has not been computed yet.
